insight.activation.guide.desc: Bright cells = highly active neurons (important). Dark cells = rarely/never active (pruning candidates). Rows are layers, columns are neurons.
insight.activation.guide.title: Heatmap reading guide
insight.activation.highDead.desc: A large fraction of neurons never activate. Pruning these can significantly reduce model size with minimal quality impact.
insight.activation.highDead.title: {pct}% dead neurons detected
insight.activation.lowDead.desc: Most neurons are well-utilized. Aggressive pruning may hurt quality — proceed carefully.
insight.activation.lowDead.title: Only {pct}% dead neurons
insight.activation.medDead.desc: Some neurons are inactive. Moderate pruning potential — simulate before committing.
insight.activation.medDead.title: {pct}% dead neurons
insight.activation.needProfile.desc: Run a few inference passes to capture which neurons are active. This data drives the heatmap and enables pruning.
insight.activation.needProfile.title: Generate an activation profile first
insight.arch.compact.desc: Small enough for iPhones and iPads. Fast inference, good for chat and simple tasks.
insight.arch.compact.title: Compact model ({params}B params)
insight.arch.fullprec.desc: At {size} GB, 4-bit quantization can reduce size by ~75%.
insight.arch.fullprec.title: Full precision (not quantized)
insight.arch.gqa.desc: GQA reduces KV cache memory — already optimized for longer conversations on edge.
insight.arch.gqa.title: Grouped Query Attention ({ratio}:1)
insight.arch.highbit.desc: Could be further compressed to 4-bit to roughly halve size with minimal quality loss.
insight.arch.highbit.title: {bits}-bit — room to compress
insight.arch.large.desc: High quality but needs 16GB+ RAM. Consider quantization or pruning to fit smaller devices.
insight.arch.large.title: Large model ({params}B params)
insight.arch.midsize.desc: Best quality-to-size ratio. Fits most Macs and high-end iPads. Good for coding, reasoning, and complex tasks.
insight.arch.midsize.title: Mid-size model ({params}B params)
insight.arch.moe.desc: Only a subset of experts activate per token. Cold experts can be pruned to save space.
insight.arch.moe.title: Mixture of Experts model
insight.arch.noProfile.desc: Generate one to unlock pruning simulation, auto-optimizer, and dead neuron detection.
insight.arch.noProfile.title: No activation profile loaded
insight.arch.quantized.desc: {size} GB on disk — good balance of size and quality. Further compression via pruning is still possible.
insight.arch.quantized.title: Already {bits}-bit quantized
insight.attention.needTrace.desc: Go to Inference Tracer, enable "Capture attention weights", then run a prompt. The patterns will appear here.
insight.attention.needTrace.title: Run inference with attention capture first
insight.attention.optHint.desc: Layers dominated by LOCAL patterns are good candidates for sliding window attention optimization. SINK-heavy layers should be preserved.
insight.attention.optHint.title: Optimization hint
insight.attention.patterns.desc: SINK = attends to first token (memory anchor). LOCAL = attends to nearby tokens (sliding window). GLOBAL = attends broadly (context integration). SPARSE = selective attention.
insight.attention.patterns.title: Pattern types explained
insight.autoOpt.howItWorks.desc: Searches combinations of pruning thresholds, bit-widths, and layer removal to find Pareto-optimal configurations that balance size and quality.
insight.autoOpt.howItWorks.title: How it works
insight.autoOpt.needProfile.desc: The auto-optimizer searches the pruning+quantization space using activation data. Load a profile first.
insight.autoOpt.needProfile.title: Activation profile required
insight.autoOpt.targetDevice.desc: Choose the device you want to deploy on — the optimizer will filter for configurations that fit within its memory.
insight.autoOpt.targetDevice.title: Select a target device
insight.autoTune.cached.desc: Once tuned, results are saved to disk. Re-running for the same model+device will be instant.
insight.autoTune.cached.title: Results are cached
insight.autoTune.largeModel.desc: Each configuration requires a full inference pass. With a large model, the search may take several minutes.
insight.autoTune.largeModel.title: Large model — tuning may take a while
insight.autoTune.what.desc: Searches KV cache sizes, temperatures, and batch sizes to find the fastest configuration for your specific device + model combination.
insight.autoTune.what.title: What auto-tune optimizes
insight.batch.saved.desc: Each optimized model is saved to a new directory alongside the original. Nothing is overwritten.
insight.batch.saved.title: Results are saved
insight.batch.workflow.desc: Add multiple models, select an operation (quantize, prune, vocab prune), and run all at once. Great for optimizing a model family.
insight.batch.workflow.title: Production workflow
insight.benchmark.compare.desc: Add the original model and its optimized variants. Key metrics: tokens/second (speed), perplexity (quality), disk size (deployment).
insight.benchmark.compare.title: What to compare
insight.benchmark.export.desc: Use the CSV export to share benchmark results with your team or include in documentation.
insight.benchmark.export.title: Export results
insight.chat.largeModel.desc: At {size} GB, first-token latency may be noticeable. Consider optimizing for faster inference.
insight.chat.largeModel.title: Large model — slower responses expected
insight.chat.stt.desc: Upload audio to transcribe. Supports chunked processing for long recordings.
insight.chat.stt.title: Speech-to-Text model
insight.chat.tts.desc: Type text to generate speech. Use the audio player to listen to results.
insight.chat.tts.title: Text-to-Speech model
insight.chat.vision.desc: This model can understand images. Try pasting or uploading an image in your message.
insight.chat.vision.title: Vision-Language model
insight.comparison.beforeAfter.desc: Load the original model as primary and the optimized version as comparison. The diff highlights what changed — parameters, layer count, size reduction.
insight.comparison.beforeAfter.title: Before vs After optimization
insight.comparison.latency.desc: Run inference on both models first (via Inference Tracer) to enable per-layer latency comparison.
insight.comparison.latency.title: Latency comparison
insight.distill.alternatives.desc: Quantization and pruning are faster and often sufficient. Try those before investing in distillation (which requires training data and GPU time).
insight.distill.alternatives.title: Alternatives first
insight.distill.bestPractice.desc: Use the current model as teacher, pick a smaller architecture as student. Quality depends on training data quality and training duration.
insight.distill.bestPractice.title: Best practice
insight.distill.what.desc: Trains a smaller "student" model to mimic a larger "teacher". The student learns the teacher's behavior patterns, not just the raw data.
insight.distill.what.title: What distillation does
insight.export.checkDevice.desc: iPhones support ≤ 3.8 GB, iPads ≤ 10 GB. GGUF export with further quantization may be needed for mobile.
insight.export.checkDevice.title: Model is {size} GB — check target device
insight.export.vision.desc: Vision-language models need an export path that preserves image inputs. Use an integration format that your target runtime supports.
insight.export.vision.title: Vision model export
insight.inference.gguf.desc: Inference tracing is only available for MLX models. GGUF models run through a separate runtime.
insight.inference.gguf.title: GGUF models use llama.cpp
insight.inference.thinking.desc: This model supports chain-of-thought reasoning. Enable "thinking mode" to see the model's internal reasoning steps.
insight.inference.thinking.title: Thinking mode available
insight.inference.whatYouSee.desc: Token-by-token generation with probability scores. Enable timing to see per-layer latency — useful for identifying bottleneck layers.
insight.inference.whatYouSee.title: What you'll see
insight.kvCache.chart.desc: The memory curve shows total RAM needed at each context length. The device capacity bars show which devices can handle which context lengths.
insight.kvCache.chart.title: Reading the chart
insight.kvCache.gqa.desc: With {kvHeads} KV heads (vs {attnHeads} attention heads), cache grows slower — enabling longer conversations on limited RAM.
insight.kvCache.gqa.title: GQA reduces cache memory
insight.kvCache.mha.desc: Each attention head maintains its own cache. Context length will be memory-limited on mobile devices.
insight.kvCache.mha.title: Full MHA = larger KV cache
insight.merge.strategy.desc: SLERP: smooth interpolation (safest). TIES: task-specific merging (best for diverse specializations). Linear: simple weighted average.
insight.merge.strategy.title: Strategy guide
insight.merge.validate.desc: Merged models can have unpredictable quality. Always benchmark before deploying.
insight.merge.validate.title: Validate after merge
insight.merge.when.desc: Merging combines strengths of different fine-tunes. Best when models share the same base architecture but specialize in different tasks.
insight.merge.when.title: When to merge models
insight.mixedPrec.recommended.desc: Keep first 2 and last 2 layers at 8-bit. Set middle layers to 4-bit or even 3-bit. This often achieves better quality than uniform quantization at the same average bits.
insight.mixedPrec.recommended.title: Recommended approach
insight.mixedPrec.selective.desc: Not all layers need the same bit-width. Early and late layers often benefit from higher precision, while middle layers can tolerate more compression.
insight.mixedPrec.selective.title: Selective precision
insight.moe.coldExperts.desc: Experts that are rarely or never activated can be removed with minimal quality impact — this is the easiest optimization for MOE models.
insight.moe.coldExperts.title: Cold experts = free compression
insight.moe.utilization.desc: The heatmap shows which experts handle which tokens. Uneven distribution means some experts are underused and could be pruned.
insight.moe.utilization.title: Expert utilization
insight.optAdvisor.needProfile.desc: Without activation data, suggestions are based on model structure only. Load a profile for data-driven pruning recommendations.
insight.optAdvisor.needProfile.title: Profile unlocks better suggestions
insight.optAdvisor.priority.desc: High-priority suggestions have the best effort-to-benefit ratio. Start with those and validate quality after each step.
insight.optAdvisor.priority.title: Priority guide
insight.pipeline.gguf.desc: GGUF models are already optimized. Most pipeline operations require MLX safetensors format.
insight.pipeline.gguf.title: GGUF model — pipeline limited
insight.pipeline.order.desc: Quantization first (biggest size reduction), then neuron pruning (refine), then vocab pruning (optional). Layer removal is a last resort.
insight.pipeline.order.title: Recommended order
insight.pruning.howItWorks.desc: Neurons with low activation are candidates for removal. The threshold slider controls sensitivity — lower = more aggressive pruning, higher = more conservative.
insight.pruning.howItWorks.title: How pruning works
insight.pruning.needProfile.desc: Pruning simulation needs activation data to identify which neurons are safe to remove.
insight.pruning.needProfile.title: Activation profile required
insight.pruning.protectLayers.desc: First and last layers often carry disproportionate importance. Consider protecting them using the protected layers list.
insight.pruning.protectLayers.title: Protect important layers
insight.pruning.validate.desc: Always run a quality check (perplexity test) after pruning to confirm acceptable quality.
insight.pruning.validate.title: Validate after pruning
insight.quality.lowBit.desc: At {bits}-bit, some quality degradation is expected. If PPL increases more than 10-15%, consider using 4-bit instead.
insight.quality.lowBit.title: Low-bit model — check quality carefully
insight.quality.quickVsFull.desc: Quick PPL gives a fast estimate. Full Report runs multiple texts and generates sample outputs for manual inspection — use this before shipping.
insight.quality.quickVsFull.title: Quick PPL vs Full Report
insight.quality.whatPpl.desc: Lower perplexity = better predictions. A PPL of 5 means the model is roughly "5-way confused" at each token. Compare before/after optimization to measure quality impact.
insight.quality.whatPpl.title: What perplexity means
insight.weight.fitsMobile.desc: Compact enough for mobile. Ready to export.
insight.weight.fitsMobile.title: {size} GB — fits iPhone & iPad
insight.weight.largeVocab.desc: Vocab pruning removes unused tokens — effective for single-language deployments.
insight.weight.largeVocab.title: Large vocabulary ({size}K tokens)
insight.weight.mostQuantized.desc: Vast majority compressed. Remaining float tensors (embeddings, norms) are expected.
insight.weight.mostQuantized.title: {pct}% of tensors quantized
insight.weight.noQuantized.desc: 4-bit quantization can reduce size by ~75% with minimal quality loss.
insight.weight.noQuantized.title: No tensors quantized
insight.weight.partialQuantized.desc: Some layers in full precision. Full quantization could further reduce size.
insight.weight.partialQuantized.title: {pct}% quantized — partial
insight.weight.tooLarge.desc: iPhones ≤ 3.8 GB, iPads ≤ 10 GB. Quantization + pruning needed.
insight.weight.tooLarge.title: {size} GB — too large for mobile

kv.askPlaceholder: Ask about KV strategy / device fit / GQA…
kv.breakdown.title: Memory breakdown
kv.contextCards.title: Memory at common context lengths
kv.deviceTable.title: Device capacity
kv.fallbackChartHint: KV computed from model.config (backend report unavailable)
kv.dsr.callout: ⚠️ tested: small budget (2K) gave 92% recall vs 75% at 4K — smaller can be more accurate
kv.dsr.title: DSR budget recommendations (per device)
kv.hybridBannerDesc: Only {full}/{total} layers run full self-attention; the rest use linear/GDN with constant-size SSM state. The backend assumes uniform full-attn, so its KV numbers are roughly {ratio}× too high. The "corrected" lines and cards below adjust for this.

tour.step1.content: This tool helps you understand, analyze, optimize, and deploy large language models on Apple Silicon devices. Let's take a quick tour of the key features.
tour.step1.title: Welcome to Edge Studio!
tour.step2.content: Start by loading a model using the 'Open...' button in the sidebar, or browse the Model Hub to download from HuggingFace. The tool supports any MLX-compatible model.
tour.step2.title: Loading a Model
tour.step3.content: Visualize your model's structure as an interactive tree. See layer counts, parameter sizes, and how the model is organized — embeddings, transformer blocks, and output heads.
tour.step3.title: Architecture Browser
tour.step4.content: Explore every tensor in the model — data types, sizes, distributions. Click any tensor to see full statistics including histograms. Great for understanding quantization effects.
tour.step4.title: Weight Analysis
tour.step5.content: Run inference and trace what happens at each layer. See token probabilities, attention patterns, layer contributions, and per-layer latency. Essential for understanding model behavior.
tour.step5.title: Inference Tracer
tour.step6.content: Have a real-time conversation with your model. Tokens stream in as they're generated. Adjust temperature, top-k, and other parameters to see how they affect output quality.
tour.step6.title: Chat
tour.step7.content: The Optimizer suggests quantization, pruning, and other optimizations. The Auto Optimizer searches for the best configuration that fits your target device. Pipeline chains multiple operations together.
tour.step7.title: Optimization Tools
tour.step8.content: Export your model to GGUF for llama.cpp, CoreML for Apple devices, or generate Swift code for direct integration. You can also generate HTML reports of your analysis.
tour.step8.title: Export & Deploy
